record.original_question: How can the wild McKay correspondence and motivic integration over wild Deligne-Mumford stacks be related to other theories of wild ramification?

evidence.quote: Problem 11.1. Relate the wild McKay correspondence and motivic integration over wild Deligne-Mumford stacks with other theories on wild ramification.

artifact.category_tag: wild McKay correspondence and motivic integration
artifact.status_search_result: The problem is posed as a broad programmatic open question linking the wild McKay correspondence (developed by Wood–Yasuda, Tonini–Yasuda and others) with classical wild ramification theories. No comprehensive solution is known; partial connections (e.g., interpretations via Artin/Swan-type conductors) exist within the wild McKay correspondence itself, but a full bridge to Abbes–Saito theory or characteristic cycles remains open as of available literature.

status_evidence.title: Motivic integration over wild Deligne-Mumford stacks (Yasuda)
status_evidence.snippet: Problem 11.1 asks to relate the wild McKay correspondence and motivic integration over wild Deligne-Mumford stacks with other theories on wild ramification.
status_evidence.claim: Stated explicitly as an open problem.
